clue.text: While up at uni, having entered it ends somehow being brought to light

indicators.note: done somehow means done in no fixed way, so the letters that follow are rearranged
one phrase going in through a door means it sits inside the other, so the student phrase sits within the shuffled letters

parts.note: the six letters of these two words, rearranged and split around the inserted part
while a student is up at university, they are in term

explanation.surface: A student coming up to university finds that things somehow come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TERM is the phrase for 'while up at uni'; it goes into the middle of the shuffled IT ENDS, DIS...ENT, to give DISINTERMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterment is digging something up from the grave, the act of unearthing it into daylight.

clue.text: Native American ornament, charm created fancily

indicators.note: something made fancily is made in an elaborate, rearranged way, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: the twelve letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Native American ornament, perhaps a charm, made with some elaborate craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamcatcher is a hoop with a woven web and feathers, an Ojibwe charm hung to filter bad dreams.

clue.text: Safeguard helping to pressure tyres

indicators.note: the letters help to make up the words that follow, so they are found spanning them

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tip for safe motoring: keeping tyres properly inflated protects you.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a guarantee or security against loss, something that protects a lender or promise.

clue.text: Turbulent lives beset by trouble locally

indicators.note: to be beset by something is to be surrounded by it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: noy is a dialect word for annoy or trouble; locally flags the regional word
to live is to be, so lives gives is

explanation.surface: A life of turmoil spent surrounded by local troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word: noy, short for annoy, survives in regional English.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent can describe a loud, disorderly crowd or scene, full of uproar and clamour.

clue.text: Haulier's strap, once very small, surrounding form of lump

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version of it reshaped, so its letters are reordered
one word surrounding another wraps around it, so the shuffled letters go inside

parts.note: tine is an old word for tiny; once flags an obsolete usage
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny old strap wrapped around some lumpy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete word: tine, meaning tiny, appears in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumpline is a band across the forehead or chest used by porters to carry or haul heavy loads.

clue.text: Spells you may find nurse treated

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on and altered, so the word's letters are reordered

parts.note: the five letters of this word

explanation.surface: Magic spells a nurse might use on a patient being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are ancient letters and also magical charms or incantations, so they serve as spells.

clue.text: Metheglin? Crazy about the heart of it

definitions.note: definition by example: metheglin is one kind of the answer

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the letter that follows

parts.note: a direct synonym
it points back to the first word of the clue, Metheglin, whose central letter is E

explanation.surface: A drinker going mad over the essence of a spiced old Welsh brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the clue's own first word, Metheglin; its middle (fifth of nine) letter E goes inside MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Metheglin is a spiced or medicated honey drink from Wales, a particular type of fermented honey wine.

clue.text: Laughing hyena may account for such an antelope with a neigh!

indicators.note: the jumbled phrase accounts for both the answer and the neigh together, its letters reshuffled between them

parts.note: all thirteen letters, to be rearranged
these letters are what is left over once the answer is taken out

explanation.surface: A laughing hyena and a neighing beast lumped together might make some odd antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: LAUGHING HYENA = NYLGHAU + A NEIGH, so remove the neigh's letters from the jumble to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nylghau, or nilgai, is a large Indian antelope, the bluebuck.

clue.text: Insect order in peony that's intrigued artist

indicators.note: intrigued is read as schemed over or plotted, so the preceding letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these words, rearranged
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter fascinated by an insect found in a peony flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Thysanoptera is the taxonomic order of thrips, tiny fringe-winged insects often found on flowers.

clue.text: Once in a brawl, completely involved in endless stir

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: to stir someone is to rouse them
as in out and out, fully

explanation.surface: Someone fully caught up in a brawl that keeps on stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the answer as obsolete, an old legal adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Routous was an old legal term for taking part in a rout, an unlawful riotous assembly or affray.

clue.text: Something to bind old thong? Jock's in a tangle

definitions.note: Jock’s marks it as a Scots word

parts.note: taw is an old word for a leather thong or whip
a tie binds things together

explanation.surface: A Scotsman muddled about what to tie an old thong with.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the opposite order to the clue: TAW then TIE. Jock is a nickname for a Scot, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, tawtie means matted or tangled, used of hair or wool that is knotted together.

clue.text: More than half Italian fizzy drink is dull

definitions.note: verb phrase: to prose is to speak or write tediously

indicators.note: only more than half of the word is used, so its tail is cut off

parts.note: the Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A complaint that a sparkling Italian wine has gone flat when half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Five of the eight letters of PROSECCO are kept. As a verb, to prose is to talk on boringly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prose is to discourse in a tedious, uninspired way, which is to be boring as a speaker or writer.

clue.text: Unfriendly Scots frequently object

definitions.note: Scots marks it as a Scots word

parts.note: a dictionary abbreviation for frequently
an object, or goal, is an aim

explanation.surface: A complaint that Scottish people often object to things.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraim, a Scots form of fremd, means strange or foreign, hence cold and unfriendly towards someone.

clue.text: Called back on being dismissed by herald, bad-tempered

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: called on the phone

indicators.note: the little word is sent away from the longer one, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: the Lord Lyon is Scotland's chief herald
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A herald, irritably called back and then sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: RANG reversed gives GNAR; LYON loses ON to leave LY. The Lord Lyon King of Arms heads Scottish heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarly in Chambers can mean ill-natured or crabbed, like a gnarled old branch, so grumpy and irritable.

clue.text: Pottery first to last lined up as before

definitions.note: as before marks an obsolete word

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front of the word to its end

explanation.walkthrough: The W of WARE moves to the end. AREW is Spenser's word for 'in a row'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arew is an archaic adverb meaning in a row or in order, things placed one after another.

clue.text: Pariahs, reverse of lyric among gluttons

indicators.note: being among others means sitting in their midst, so one word goes inside

parts.note: a glutton is a pig

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word turned back to front

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem about outcasts recited backwards to a crowd of gluttons.
explanation.walkthrough: Pariahs here are the animals, pariah dogs, not social outcasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-dogs, or pi-dogs, are the ownerless half-wild dogs of Asian towns, also called pariah dogs.

clue.text: Very small Scotch, extreme in goodness!

definitions.note: Scotch marks it as a Scots word

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: my! is an exclamation like goodness!
OTT, over the top, means extreme

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a tiny but extremely good Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' tempts as whisky, but here it flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Motty is Scots for full of motes, specks of dust, so describing tiny particles.

clue.text: Number that's designed at the edges or with scalloped borders

indicators.note: one word at the edges of another forms its outside, so the other sits within

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' tempts as the definition, but it is just the abbreviation sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crenated describes a leaf or shell edge notched with rounded teeth, like a scalloped border.

clue.text: Alexandra displaying what accompanies thrust, around centre of fashion

indicators.note: around means one part encircles the other

explanation.walkthrough: SA SA, an old fencing exclamation heard in Shakespeare, goes around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sasha is the familiar Russian pet form of Alexander and Alexandra.

clue.text: Pressure on head of edible fungus forced up part of primary growth

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

parts.note: its opening letter
the morel is an edible fungus

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the pressure symbol on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the plerome is the central tissue of a growing tip, from which the stele of the primary body develops.

clue.text: Displaced relation of some Austrians

explanation.surface: A displaced family member of some Austrian people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirolean means belonging to the Tirol, an alpine region in western Austria, so relating to its people.

clue.text: Memorizes major role in play, not specified

clue.text: Bovine lady's confused about hawkish bird

clue.text: Where one lands or departs, adjacent to capital

clue.text: Old ewe with bit of tangled hair covering hoof

parts.note: its opening letter

clue.text: Sudden round of applause — it helps to avoid offence
